summary: # Marvelous Designer Tutorial: Dress Making - Making the Skirt Hem In this section, we will explore the steps required to modify a T-shirt into a dress, focusing specifically on the creation of the skirt hem. This tutorial will guide you through the technical processes using Marvelous Designer. ## Selecting the Skirt Length Next, let's make the skirt part. Start by selecting the belt and checking the specific length, then draw a circle that measures the data. 1. Select the outer line of the circle. 2. Choose the expansion of the outer line of the plate. This expansion value is the group length; it is recommended not to make it too long, as this may complicate subsequent production. 3. Remember to select the production inner line. ## Cutting the Plate After expansion, select the inner line that has just been created. In the menu located in the right-hand corner, select the conversion position. - To facilitate the arrangement of the plate, you can cut this half-circle. - Draw two inner lines to cut this plate. - Keep one side of it, and delete the other side. - Cut along the symmetrical plate. ## Arranging the Skirt Arrange each piece with a positioning ball near the virtual model. Repeat this step as needed to ensure proper alignment. - To prevent unnecessary bruising, you can freeze the sleeve version. The skirt and waist are now combined. If you are unsure of the direction, utilize the free sewing tool to point at the 3D window during the movement, then use the line sewing tool to sew the sides together. ## Simulating the Skirt After opening the simulation, you will see that the umbrella shape is complete. You can now expand the outline of the skirt to lengthen it. 1. Choose "Extend" from the side angle to extend the version along the original writing rate. 2. Verify that the outline of the skirt is complete. 3. Simulate and organize the skirt. 4. Delete the inner line and adjust the sewing line accordingly. 5. Add the line and finally expand the outline. ## Adjusting Expansion Values You can adjust the expansion value according to your needs. Be cautious—if there are more white folds, expanding the outside of the panel line again may lead to grid breakage. Since we have passed the ground, we need to fold it up to avoid unstable collisions. If you use a folding arrangement tool with broken panels, the breakage may worsen. ### Closing Ground Collision To address this, close the ground collision first: 1. In the 3D window background, right-click to select the model attribute. 2. Close the collision under the paper surface of the attribute editor. 3. Open the simulation again, and the panel line can now pass the ground. ## Finalizing the Skirt Now, let's deal with the skirt to ensure it has a collision with the ground: 1. Harden the skirt to make it firm and hold it up. 2. Apply pressure 1 to the skirt so that it can be held up bigger. 3. Open the simulation and drag the skirt out while lifting it above the ground. ### Adjusting the Simulation Attributes Return to the simulation attribute settings to open the collision for the ground. Ensure that the result is appropriate. - Use the slime tool and reduce the pressure back to 0 to end the hardening process. - If the skirt becomes hard after adjustments, you can try the process again. ## Testing Pressure Values You can also use a smaller number for pressure to maintain the expansion. Click the triangle on the left side of the pressure to enter and test various pressure values. - If there is an obvious bulge causing the fold to be lost, appropriately reduce the pressure. - At a pressure value of 0.5, you will notice a strong bulge. - Finally, select a pressure of 0.2 for a slight expansion effect. ## Creating the Pocket Shape Next, let's start shaping the pocket body of the dress: 1. Select the outermost circle of the skirt. 2. Select the inner line of the shoulder strap and input a value of 10 mm. 3. Cut and sew them to create an independent board. ### Applying Fabric and Adjusting Attributes Apply a new fabric to the edge of this circle and change the physical attribute to leather. The leather effect will turn the edge of the fabric into a curved effect with thicker sides. - Unlock and simulate all of the upper parts simultaneously. - For the waistline shape, adjust the elastic band to maintain the original shape. - When a strip or piece of area is attached to the elastic band, it will stay in shape. ## Final Adjustments Change the face of the shirt to a different fabric. After the Native cotton band is sewn, cut and paste the fabric. - Change the fabric to a different color temporarily to distinguish between the various materials. - Remember that the skirt fabric pulls the upper body down, making the seam allowance of the chest appear unnatural. - Use the edge seam tool to drag the seam allowance on the model to a lower position to create a more natural curve, and repeat this on the other side. Finally, check all other parts to ensure stability, then freeze all the fabric to complete the skirt hem modification.
